summary: Feed s146_double is degraded: IDS port overloaded to 310% capacity (3.10 Gbps bursts vs 1 Gbps port) and 8.9% duplicate traffic detected, causing packet loss risk and wasted inspection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering full aggregate bursts peaking at 3.10 Gbps in 1ms intervals to a single 1 Gbps IDS port without load-balancing or filtering, exceeding capacity by 210% across 5 intervals.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS will indiscriminately drop packets during bursts, creating blind spots where exploits/malware evade stateful detection; needs both directions and full payload but cannot keep up.

recommended_fix.why: Flow-aware load balancing across multiple 1G IDS ports/instances keeps per-port utilization below 80% threshold while preserving both directions per flow for IDS state tracking.

findings.root_cause: Broker aggregation is forwarding duplicate copies of the same packets (8.9% - 313 of 3526 packets, threshold 5%), likely from overlapping SPAN/TAP feeds or a loop without deduplication enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU/memory re-inspecting duplicates, inflates alerts and connection counts, skews analytics and reduces effective capacity already constrained by overload.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication with short window to drop identical packets before the IDS, eliminating 8.9% waste without losing unique traffic.
